question: Which instrument is used to show the direction of flow of current in a circuit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Galvanometer.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

 
• A galvanometer is a device that can **detect and measure** very** tiny currents** in an electrical circuit.
 
• A galvanometer is made up of a **needle** attached to a coil that is free to pivot within a **magnetic field** formed by the poles of one or more **permanent magnets.**
 
• A moving coil galvanometer works on the **principle of a torque** being experienced by a current-carrying coil positioned in a magnetic field.
 
• The radial field and coil springs ensure that the** deflection is proportional to the current strength.**
 
• The **sensitivity** (i.e. current sensitivity)** of a galvanometer** is defined as the angle of deflection per unit current flowing through it.
